title: Insert a Custom Type and Chain Output

blocks.text: Give a Custom Value a Representation

We will use Recuento, a record with aceptados and rechazados, both between 0 and 10. Its agreed representation is [aceptados;rechazados], in that order. The brackets and semicolon are part of the text; they are not fields of the object. A representation useful for our tests need not be every program's preferred format.

The struct has public members: the compiler does not prevent constructing values outside the domain. recuento_valido can check them. Here we construct valid values and pass them to the writer under that precondition. The next lesson will validate fields extracted from text before assigning a Recuento.

blocks.question: When writing [2;1] for a Recuento, what have we produced?
options: A copy of the object's memory, including its methods.
A representation of its fields according to an agreement.
A new object that the reader will automatically reconstruct.
blocks.explanation: We wrote interpretable characters. Reconstructing a value requires a reader that checks the agreement.

blocks.text: The Custom Operator Is Also a Function

To support destino << valor, we define a function named operator<<. Before building the writer for Recuento, consider a smaller example: Cantidad holds unidades between 0 and 5 and is represented as (unidades). The operator's first parameter is std::ostream&, and its second is const Cantidad&. Writing changes the stream; the value is only read. Returning std::ostream& passes back a reference to the same destination for continued insertion.

The function is defined alongside our type, outside namespace std. In this case, cout << resumen calls operator<<(cout, resumen). Inside, we use the familiar character and integer insertions. We do not need access to hidden representation or to turn the record into a string first.

blocks.question: What return type permits cout << resumen << " end" with the operator we just defined?
options: void, because the second insertion starts over.
Recuento, because the next insertion must modify the record.
std::ostream&, referring to the same destination received.
blocks.explanation: The second insertion receives the result of the first. It needs the stream on which writing should continue.

blocks.question: Predict the complete output for the two quantities, including the separator inserted by main.
blocks.explanation: Each insertion of the custom type returns cout. The text | is inserted between the representations of the two quantities.

blocks.question: Predict the output. Here the operator receives an ostringstream.
blocks.explanation: The operator composes (1) in captura; the string ;end continues in that same stream. main then displays the resulting string.

blocks.question: The operator returned the destination. What does that return mean?
options: It permits continuation; errors are checked in the stream's state.
It certifies that every character reached the physical file.
It clears any failure before the next insertion.
blocks.explanation: Returning the reference neither repairs nor certifies the destination. For a file, we still check writing and closing.

blocks.text: Build an Operator for Memory and File Output

Starting from the editor, define operator<< for the supplied Recuento. It must read the record without modifying it, write [aceptados;rechazados] to the borrowed destination, and return that same destination. Test fields are valid, and the streams retain their default decimal settings.

In main, create Recuento{3, 2}. Insert it into an ostringstream followed by ;end and, separately, into the relative file recuento_lgp.txt. Check opening and writing after closing. main displays Memory=[3;2];end|Saved; the file must contain only [3;2]. The operator neither uses cout internally nor adds ;end.

Also test Recuento{0, 0} and Recuento{10, 10}. Check that the fields change in both destinations, the string retains ;end, and the file does not receive it. Matching the final message without using the record does not satisfy the contract.
Create only your relative test file inside each execution. The reference appears after your attempt.

Criteria: a stream passed by modifiable reference, a record passed by const reference, characters in the agreed order, and return of the same stream. Memory and file output use the same operator; destination selection, opening, and closing belong to the caller. With 0 and 0, the visible string is Memory=[0;0];end|Saved and the file contains [0;0]. With 10 and 10, both fields become 10.

It is also valid to insert in stages and finish with return destino. Renaming the parameter does not change the contract. The operator preserves the formatting settings of the stream it receives; these tests use decimal. We have not defined serialization that is independent of every possible stream configuration.

blocks.question: Another screen needs the text 3 accepted and 2 rejected. Which organization preserves our agreed format for test files?
options: Change the operator's brackets only when the filename matches.
Create another presentation function for that purpose without changing the agreement.
Assume str() will automatically transform [3;2] into that sentence.
blocks.explanation: A shared format does not have to be used for everything. Another presentation may read the same data under its own contract.

blocks.text: Insertion and stream types are covered in the primary source (Stroustrup, 2024, section 9.6, p. 266, and sections 9.7–9.8). The model, format, and activities are original to this learning path.
